releases.displayName: Copa City: The Tutorial Revamp Patch

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/43cbc560bd9f8c09eeec9180d8c1cd03edb7d494.png"]
Hello!

We’ve got a solid new update ready for you in Copa City. We’ve been reading your feedback, and today we’re rolling out a major rework of how new players learn the ropes, alongside some much-needed quality-of-life tweaks for everyone.
Here is what’s waiting for you in the Tutorial Revamp Patch.
(Just a heads-up: Because of these big changes, old tutorial saves won't work anymore. You'll need to start a fresh tutorial run, but as always, you can skip it and jump straight into a normal game!)

We reworked the tutorial from scratch to make it more straightforward. We’ve cut the old 8 scenarios down to 4 focused stages that cleanly cover the three main parts of the game: the Building Loop, the City Management Loop, and the Stadium Loop.

Smoother Learning Curve: Dialogues and tutorial screens won't interrupt your tasks anymore. You get the context upfront, and then you're free to tackle the objectives at your own pace, actually playing the game while you learn.
Better Visual Cues: We’ve made the highlights and Points of Interest (POIs) much clearer. If you keep an eye on these on-screen cues, you'll figure out exactly what to do without getting stuck.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/3cb17d1a32a50145ea1ebe6397b5dee675d2bb36.jpg"]

notes.title: Getting a Grip on the Core Loop

items.text: The old tutorial had a few blind spots, so this one covers all the basic mechanics. Plus, we made sure to remove repetitive tasks - you’ll be dealing with fresh challenges the whole way through.

The Big Picture: The main goal here is to show you that everything you do - managing the city, fixing issues, and hyping up the event - leads to one thing: getting the biggest crowd possible safely to the stadium. You're setting the stage so match day can happen.

Stadium Mechanics Unlocked: The tutorial now walks you through the entire stadium management loop. You'll unlock stands, handle ticket sales, manage the flow of fans, and keep their needs met once they're inside.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/4682a27bbf27e5e8edcb50aec051c74f659793ce.jpg"]

More Tools, Streamlined Experience: We’ve given you access to more building modules and impactful decision-making events right off the bat, letting you immediately see how your choices shape the game. To balance this and prevent information overload, we’ve streamlined the tutorial by temporarily hiding some of the more UI parameters. This step-by-step approach allows you to comfortably master your resources and the interface at a natural pace, with advanced features gradually unlocking as you progress.
The fourth part of the tutorial acts as an epilogue to test what you've learned. You'll take on the final crowd management challenge: guiding the massive fan march through the streets to the stadium.
We also added a time-based scoring system for the tutorial. The faster and more efficiently you get things set up, the better your score.
Outside of the tutorial, we’re pushing some global changes and QoL updates.

Quest Log: We’ve added a proper Quest Log so you can easily keep track of all your active main and side missions. You can now see exactly what rewards to expect for pulling them off, as well as the consequences you'll face if you fail a task.

Introducing the Codex: Think of this as your go-to knowledge base. You can open the Codex right from the tutorial screens or normal gameplay to quickly look up how specific mechanics work and how they fit into the core game loop.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/330d13e8ff687f3e36363c371cc63c9f438fa929.png"]

The Final March: A lot of you pointed out that the victory screen used to pop up right when the crowd march was getting good. We changed that. Now, you get to actually watch the fans reach the stadium and handle all the final march missions. It’s a proper payoff for all your prep work. You can see the first march as early as Stage 4 of the tutorial, after choosing to lead the fans into the stadium yourself!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/f46e1dad60b0083f59ae8cdd1de8a99fe455c31a.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/b2aef132d0d2505d1f291b04d3f4091854b6cde0.jpg"]
Main Menu Art: We swapped in a fresh illustration for the Main Menu.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/61de5b120188c75ff74c37367aee52369fb91293.jpg"]
Better Gamepad Controls: Playing with a controller on the tutorial level feels much smoother now.
Upgraded Stadium Cameras: We tweaked the stadium camera angles in all three cities. It’s now way easier to see what you're doing and place modules when moving between different stadium sections.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/c04531d12668b926c06389fd3c69d308d636eb24.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/a528d7a66f53678045cfcdd8203a772d5bb267db.jpg"]
Standout Club Modules: Club-specific modules now look a bit more distinct in the Build Menu, making them faster to find.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/cf56089ebdf48c9bb6ed879238f176fffb3b09cc.jpg"]

Give the new patch a spin and let us know what you think. Whether you're a new player figuring things out or a veteran checking out the new endgame march, we hope this makes your time in Copa City a lot better.
Catch you on match day! The Copa City Development Team
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/1de82cd7ae02343825cbfae04b8a5613a976b4b0.png"]

notes.title: We're bringing major balance changes to the Rio Campaign!

items.text: Based on your feedback, we’ve taken a close look at the Rio Campaign - specifically Match 2 in the campaign (Copa Da Festa) - and made significant adjustments to make the main progression smoother while keeping the challenge alive for completionists. We’ve also ironed out some annoying controller and UI bugs.

notes.title: Here is everything coming in Patch 1.0.9

items.text: Rio Campaign Balance (Match 2: Copa Da Festa)
Rebalanced Objectives: Main quest lines are now smoother and easier to complete, while side quests have been tweaked to offer a stiffer challenge.
Resource & Card Tweaks: Adjusted starting resources and rebalanced card effects gained during this scenario to give you a fairer start.
New Module - Specialist Training Center: You can now build this module to regain Specialists and keep your operations running!
Quest Overhaul: Changed various quest objectives, rewards, and completion conditions across the board.
Crowd Flow Improvements
Rio Crowd Routes: We’ve shortened fan marching routes and adjusted crowd barriers. Your fans will now move through the city faster, making crowd flows much easier to track and manage.
Bug Fixes
Controller Double Input: Fixed an issue where single button presses registered twice, causing menus to skip options or close unintentionally.
Stadium Mascot Bug: Fixed a glitch where placing the Team Mascot in certain stand sockets would consume your resources without actually placing the module.
Berlin Cable Cars: Fixed pathing and visual issues with the cable cars in Westend.
UI Polish: The Berlin city logo on the main menu's stadium select screen now displays in full, glorious quality to match the other cities.
League Code: 91cs6e
See you in the city,
The Copa City Team
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/7c4e9391f40adace052effcebacd41631dc500c6.png"]

Patch 1.08 is now available to download, bringing a fresh wave of fixes and improvements to the game. This update clears out several frustrating bugs and smooths out the overall gameplay so you can enjoy your time without interruptions. Thanks to everyone who took the time to report issues and help us track down these glitches. You can check out the full list of changes and what’s new in the notes below!

FPS drops while mouse polling rate is set to 1000Hz and more: Temporary fix we found for that issue is to lower mouse polling rate on your machine (500Hz f.e), but we are actively trying to resolve the source of this issue.

Rio: Fixed the "Ultras at the Window" quest (Option B) showing a negative objective counter when modules were placed before obtaining the quest - pre-placed modules no longer count against your objectives.
Rio: Fixed only one assembly point being available in the Rio Campaign.
Berlin: Cleaned up voice-over lines across the Berlin Campaign that accidentally included duplicate actor takes.
Fixed corrupted Arsenal banners appearing after a district turned neutral - neutral districts now correctly display no banners.
Fixed the Olympique de Marseille tier 4 bonus not working - modules in OM-controlled districts now correctly provide 50% more fun.
Rio: Fixed buses appearing in random places and getting stuck — buses now spawn at their designated spots and keep moving.
Berlin: Removed unnecessary red (blocked) tiles from grids across the city, freeing up more space for module placement.
Fixed a selected module's placement ghost remaining visible after entering a different stand.
Fixed the number of fans in the crowd dropping below zero after failing enough side quests.
Fixed voice-overs being muted instead of paused when opening the Active Cards tab, which caused lines to resume without subtitles.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/dd7dd3c652270b1fd8463974f00b231a9b74eecd.png"]
City Captains,

We’ve completely reworked how Quests, Cards, and Economy interact in Campaign to make gameplay smoother, fairer, and more rewarding. The following changes apply to the first Campaign scenario (PGE Narodowy - Warsaw) - work on balancing the remaining parts of the campaign is still ongoing, and we will keep you informed as soon as they are available.
Main quests are now tuned to be gentler. Simply completing the main questline will comfortably secure a Tier 1 scenario completion.
Side quests now offer steeper challenges for players aiming to hit higher Tiers, packed with significantly boosted rewards.
Reward cards earned from completing quests are now punchier and noticeably stronger than standard cards received from reaching new MR Tiers.
Active, temporary time-based buffs (~24-hour duration) now carry stronger effects than passive cards, rewarding active tactical play.
Groundwork has been laid to bring Club Traits directly into campaign gameplay, helping teach unique club identities and creating a more cohesive management experience across all modes.
World Map Marketing: Reduced monetary costs of marketing campaigns across the world map by 25%.
MR1 Modules: Building costs reduced by 20%.
MR2 Modules: Building costs reduced by 20% | Base Revenue increased by 20%.
MR3 Modules: Building costs reduced by 10% | Base Revenue increased by 10%.
MR4 Modules: Base Revenue adjusted down by 20% to curb extreme late-game economy inflation.
Ultrabite Snack Stand: Received an additional dedicated revenue boost!
Pacing & Matchday Readiness (MR)
MR4 Acceleration: Increased MR point generation speed at Tier MR4 by ~40% (lowered threshold from 500 fan-needs to 300 fan-needs).
Match Inspection Quest: Doubled the MR points awarded upon completion.
Fixed an issue preventing Play With Purpose 2, 3, and 4 (Ultrabite / Froozle questlines) from triggering properly.
Ultrabite (Play With Purpose 1): Adjusted counters, lowered required Core Fans to 500, and updated objective text to clearly display the required module to build.
Besiktas Ultras Sector Request: Extended the time limit to give managers more breathing room.
Team Arrivals Quest: Clarified unlocking cable cars station objectives to streamline progression.

In this patch, we’ve also focused on squashing reported bugs, sharpening controller inputs during tutorials, fixing stadium visual overlaps, and refining crowd count calculations to keep your matchday running as smoothly as possible.

releases.displayName: An Important Update Regarding Copa City’s Pricing and Future

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/32d5f0fe955457d2d27473b04c73df34e4f12266.jpg"]
Hi everyone,

It has been one week since the launch of Copa City. As this is our very first game, we want to start by thanking you for your support, engagement, and the invaluable feedback you’ve shared in your reviews - it means the world to us and shows us exactly what we need to improve. We released the game with great ambitions, aiming to bring a fresh perspective to the football gaming genre. However, the initial wave of negative reviews made it clear that the experience didn't satisfy the expectations. We have spent this past week actively updating the game and closely analyzing your feedback to understand exactly where we need to make adjustments.
Plain and simple, we could boil all the negative reviews to these points:
A tedious, mandatory tutorial and early campaign softlocks.
UI transparency and vague task instructions made it hard to understand the mechanics.
Frustrating failure mechanics that cut gameplay short without warning.
Mismatch between expectations and reality of the gameplay.

Looking at these rough edges, we have to admit that we were too optimistic with the initial price tag. The current state of the game just doesn't justify it yet. We love this project, and this is our honest attempt to make things right, lower the barrier of entry, and - most importantly - rebuild your trust. Effective today, we are permanently lowering the base price of Copa City on Steam with changes to other platforms pricing on their way.

However, it’s not all bad. Over the last 7 days, we’ve been listening, rolling out fixes, and watching a dedicated core of players dive deep into the actual systems of Copa City. Seeing you master the matchdays despite the onboarding hurdles shows us that the core game we built is worth fighting for.
Steam Players: Valve will be refunding the price difference directly to the Steam Wallets of everyone who already purchased the game at the higher price point.
We are not giving up on this game. We want to continue developing this project, and we deeply appreciate the support we’ve received from those of you who see the potential in what we’re building.

Copa City is our first commercial release and we are honored and humbled that you trusted us and purchased our game. We are currently working on important changes to the game's structure, onboarding and game modes. We want to take the parts you enjoy the most and flesh them out to provide the best football match organization game possible.
Next Days: Another batch of stability fixes, the launch of our Online Wiki to help you with the game systems, and possibility to start the campaign without completing tutorial.
July: UI overhauls + "Chairman Pass" free content update - our response to the community members who asked for more relaxed and free experience.
August: In-game Codex System, a brand-new tutorial, and further UI polish.

We will continue to roll out bug fixes and general polish updates on a regular basis. To track our progress, check the upcoming Wiki for live status updates on these commitments. Regular updates are also coming directly to Steam News and our social media channels.

The promised Fluminense and Panathinaikos DLCs are still in active development. However, we want to make sure the foundation of Copa City is rock solid before expanding. Our priority is fixing the base game first, and we will roll out the DLCs only when the core experience is where it needs to be.
— The Copa City Team

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/32b85bbbd100c51271d8d16fa38d84b7b4171ce2.png"]Today's update introduces a series of important fixes and improvements aimed at eliminating bugs and enhancing the overall stability of the game. The patch covers a wide range of game aspects:
Interface localization issues and other strange information that sometimes popped up on the UI.
Audio getting a bit of love, mostly regarding voice-overs and dialogues.

Hello everyone!

We are constantly monitoring your feedback and working to make the gameplay as comfortable, smooth, and satisfying as possible. Today, we are releasing a new update that eliminates a few technical hiccups, improves overall stability, and introduces minor visual polishes.
In this batch of fixes, we focused primarily on the tactical map's performance when playing with a controller, streamlining the save system, and tidying up the user interface (UI) elements.
Below you will find the full list of changes that are currently making their way into the game:
\\[Tactical Map] Fixed focus on the filters panel.
Changed the locker room module icon.
General UI/UX fixes on grids.
Placeholder text removed and replaced with the correct content.
General save-system fixes.
Removed SFX and ambient sounds that were sometimes triggered on the loading screen.
Thank you for every report, constructive criticism, and invaluable help in catching minor and major bugs. Your feedback allows us to react quickly and constantly improve the game.
If you encounter any issues after downloading the update, please let us know in the Steam discussion section or on our official Discord server.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/c44bcdd6ed0711f374ff495cbb56fc6a88ddd593.jpg"]Thank you for sharing your initial thoughts, reviews, and detailed bug reports with us since the launch of Copa City. Having a live, active community means we have the direct player feedback needed to see exactly how the game lives up to the expectations. We are taking this feedback seriously and are immediately focusing our efforts on refining the experience and delivering a better game.

While we are excited to see players diving into the matchday logistics, we recognize that the initial onboarding experience has been bumpy for many of you. A large number of the technical issues and friction points reported were a direct result of players getting stuck or feeling lost without clear direction on what to do next. We are sorry for the frustration this caused, we are working on smoothing out the onboarding and the new update allows you to start a Single Match mode without finishing the tutorial in the Campaign mode.

Our philosophy moving forward is straightforward: we are reading your reports, we are analyzing where the progression blocks occur, and we are getting straight to work to make the gameplay loops clearer and more intuitive.
Today's patch focuses on stabilization, fixing blockers, unlocking requested features, and cleaning up UI elements.

Looking ahead, a few players recently pitched a great idea to us, and we are already working on incorporating an option we codenamed 'Chairman Pass'. We are shaping it into something we think you will really enjoy, giving you more freedom to play exactly how you want. It will be coming in the near future, and we will share more details soon.
The complete list of fixes and changes included in today's update can be found below.
Single Match mode is now unlocked even when the Campaign tutorial is not finished.
UI/UX: Fixed missing illustrations and corrected placeholder text on Match Report.
UI/UX: Fixed incorrect atlas usage in notification assets.
UI/UX: Fixed UI card issues, back button functionality in card selection, and a bug causing a blocker during card selection.
UI/UX: Removed the feedback button from the main menu.
UI/UX: Updated main menu jersey assets.
UI/UX: Added new loading screens and updated the game credits.
Gameplay & Infrastructure: Fixed issues with broken district takeovers and the branding system.
Gameplay & Infrastructure: Corrected pavement categorization; pavements and generators have been moved back to the Business, Fun, Safety, and Catering categories.
Gameplay & Infrastructure: Disabled the Crowd Management Panel.
Gameplay & Infrastructure: Fixed saving functionality regarding card modifiers.
Campaign & Quests: Implemented various quest fixes, a fix for the district loss tutorial, and resolved the Maracana locker room issue.
Graphics & Assets: Added missing Bayern Munich banners across maps.
Graphics & Assets: Fixed Jumbotron display issues.
Audio: Fixed a bug where a clicking sound would continue to play while moving the camera.
Audio: Fixed voice-over assets.
Performance & Optimization: Implemented core fixes for crowd behavior, general game balancing, and system saving.
Controls: Fixed double input issues on consoles and a specific double input bug that occurred while the Stewards Recruitment Room module window was open.

releases.displayName: Closed Beta Update: Moving Launch to January 2026

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/9926a0462d1222304c7a6f1cb8c28be8aade6cc7.png"]
To ensure we deliver the best experience possible, we have made an adjustment to our Closed Beta timeline. We are moving the Closed Beta launch to the second half of January 2026.
We believe in maintaining full transparency with our community, so we want to share the exact reasons behind this decision.
We recently received the results from our latest round of playtests. The good news is that in many areas, Copa City feels great and the gameplay loop is satisfying.
However, the results also highlighted a few key areas that unfortunately, are just not there yet.
This Beta will be your very first hands-on experience with Copa City, and we respect the golden rule of game development: you only get one chance to make a first impression.

While it hurts to delay this, we are doing so to dedicate these extra few weeks to final polishing. We simply don’t want to ruin the experience for you with rough edges that we have the power to fix right now.
